comments.author: @peterslade5085
comments.text: One evening I walked through our front door, having been to see the doctor for the umpteenth time and announced to my wife that I had been diagnosed with yet another autoimmune condition. She immediately said, “Were quitting work,  buying a caravan and a diesel Ute and we’re doing the big lap before it’s too late. And we did. It took us 18 months to complete the lap. It was the adventure of a lifetime.  We shared the driving. Made new friends, learnt to take things slowly, and renovated our headspace. There never was one single time on the sojourn when  time and the wind stopped  and my being was touched or altered in some way. It happened often . Australia sneaks up on you in its vastness.

replies.author: @HappyTravel99
replies.text: What an incredibly moving story. ❤️ Your wife's words and the decision you made together are truly inspiring. Eighteen months on the road, discovering Australia, making new friends, and finding a new perspective on life — that's something no amount of money can buy. We especially love what you said about Australia quietly touching your soul through its vastness. That's such a beautiful way to describe this extraordinary land. Thank you for sharing such a personal and meaningful chapter of your lives with us. We sincerely wish you and your wife good health, happiness, and many more wonderful adventures together. ❤️

We really appreciate your correction and will pay closer attention to these geographical details in future documentaries!

replies.author: @zalired8925
replies.text:
Best parts of Melbourne and Sydney are the rods heading out. Might as well be in any city in Europe or USA/Canada. You can only find the true Australia on the roads with no signs and the coastal and country towns no one knows exist except those who live there but will see a visitor as a new friend.. The "must see" tourist towns like Byron Bay and Margaret River in WA see tourists as nothing more than walking dollar signs and compete in who can get the most from you. 
  And head south down the coast from Sydney to Melbourne along the Princes Hwy not the bland hypnotic Hume freeway. It'll take about 3 or 4 days instead of 9 hours straight down the Hume but you'll see a month's worth of Australia instead of 5 minutes of the same sights as 200k down the road.
  In other words, whatever the glossy vouchers and social media tell you to visit showing you perfect photos or videos that took 6 months of waiting for the right conditions to make with someone saying yeh just another day here. Don't bother, the letdown always disapoints. They don't say how long until the next postcard day and hope you don't ask. And every tourist is told how unusual the weather has been lately, was perfect up until 2 days before you arrived.
